root.name: Sicilian Defense: Löwenthal Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 e5

overview: Black kicks the d4 knight with ...e5, so White plays 5.Nb5 a6 6.Nd6+ Bxd6 7.Qxd6 Qf6 and then 8.Qd1 or 8.Qxf6. Black has the bishop pair and development for a slight weakness on d6; White has an easy game and a small edge. The queen swap leads to a quiet endgame-like position with little attacking play.

white_ideas.idea: 5.Nb5 a6 6.Nd6+ Bxd6 7.Qxd6 and exploit the d6 square
Trade queens with Qxf6 to reach a quiet, slightly better ending
Develop with Nc3 and control d5, play for a knight outpost

black_ideas.idea: Bishop pair and open lines in return for the ceded bishop
Gain a tempo against the knight on b5 with ...a6 and ...Nge7
Use the d6 hole by ...Qf6 and ...Nge7 or ...d6

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on d7 and e5, White pawn on e4; a hole at d5 and a half-open c-file

character.notes: Quiet after the queen exchange or 8.Qd1; not especially sharp or solid. I am unsure.

soundness.notes: Playable for Black; White is a little better but it is not refuted.

structure.notes: Sicilian with Black e5 pawn, a half-open c-file; semi-open.

approach.notes: Offbeat: strong players seldom choose the Löwenthal as Black.

level.notes: Understanding of the bishop pair and weak squares.

sublines_that_differ.name: 5...a6 6.Nd6+ Bxd6 7.Qxd6 Qf6 8.Qxf6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 e5 5. Nb5 a6 6. Nd6+ Bxd6 7. Qxd6 Qf6 8. Qxf6
sublines_that_differ.how: Queenless middlegame where White has a small edge.

character.reason: Quiet lines with no attacks for either side.

soundness.reason: White is slightly better but Black is not in danger.

plans.reason: Black takes the bishop pair, White has the d5 and d6 squares.
